per_shot.note: Chunky amber segmented serpent bursting from the wall with a white-hot mouth; reads as a threat at play size and sits in the VEIL hue, but its spill on the tunnel rock is a soft general haze rather than a pool around the head.

Segments read as hollow stacked cones or funnels, not a body. The head has no jaw or mandible shape beyond a glow blob, and the light it throws on the adjacent blocks is weak for how bright the mouth is.

Violet crystal crab with an open pincer maw clings to the wall and reads as a creature at play size; the violet matches the amethyst ore as a deliberate accent, but its halo is a grey-white smudge that barely tints the rock.
The jaws read well. The plates are flat, saturated plastic-violet; the legs are dark indigo cut-outs with no glow; the light it puts on the wall face is neutral grey, not crystal-coloured.

Two thin tan stick figures lost in a uniformly orange core chamber. They have the same value and hue as the pillars and background, so a 'pursuer made of light' reads as dim and small and is not a threat.

The bodies read as matte faceted stone with a white diamond chest and ember sparks, not as beings of light. The dark aura behind them is the only thing that separates them, and they light nothing around them.

A cyan origami flock with bright cores, firmly inside the CRYOS hue, and its glow lands hard on the floor and wall. This is the closest to the 10-creatures ribbon; the floor-edge hotspot is close to blown out.

The faceted paper-crystal wings are clean and low-poly, with a strong cold wash on the blocks. They read as beautiful but more ambient than dangerous, and the floor top edge goes to a flat cyan stripe.

top_issues.issue: The Kindled does not read as made of light or as a threat
top_issues.why: Its bodies are mid-value tan in a chamber that is already orange and fully lit. It is darker than its surroundings, casts no visible light, and is thin and pod-sized, so a pursuer does not register.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the body emissive and the brightest value in the frame (a white-gold core fading to amber edges), give it a real point light that pools on the floor beneath it, and make it a heavier silhouette with a clear head and reaching front end. Show it in a dark tunnel too, where its light is the event.

top_issues.issue: The Geode Mimic's glow is colourless and does not land
top_issues.why: Its halo is a neutral grey-white bloom, so the wall beside it isn't tinted violet. The legs carry no emissive, so the dangerous part is lit less than the back crystal.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint the mimic's light violet-cyan so it stains the wall and ledge. Add a faint emissive to the inner jaw and leg tips, and make the open maw the brightest point so the biting end reads first.

top_issues.issue: The Long One's segments read as hollow cones and its head lacks a shape
top_issues.why: The open-ended funnel segments look like stacked traffic cones in close-up. The head is a glow blob with no jaw form, so the threat depends entirely on brightness.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap the segments so they read as solid plated rings, taper the body to a tail, and give the head a chunky faceted jaw or mandible silhouette around the white-hot mouth.

top_issues.issue: Self-light spill is uneven across the set
top_issues.why: Only the Rimewings convincingly light the rock around them. The others rely on bloom on the creature itself, which goes against 'glow that lands'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each creature a coloured point light sized to its body that visibly pools on the nearest rock faces, matching the Rimewings' and Warden's treatment.

top_issues.why: The top edge of the floor under the flock goes to a flat saturated cyan stripe. That loses the block faceting and flattens footing readability right where the player stands.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lower the flock's light intensity or raise its falloff so the floor shows a gradient pool with visible block edges, not a band.

protect: The Rimewings: cyan origami flock, bright cores, and a cold wash that lands on the CRYOS rock
The Long One's amber, chunky, faceted plating and white-hot mouth emerging from the wall
The Mimic's open pincer maw and crab silhouette on the wall, and its violet tying it to the amethyst ore
Every creature stays low-poly, flat-faceted and free of texture noise
The dark aura behind the Kindled as a separation device, if it is kept once the body becomes emissive
